_comment: FROZEN Phase-6 analysis rules — the single numeric authority for the visual/audio/hook analyzers. boundsSha256 (the digest of this document's canonical JSON, `_comment` excluded) is an input to every componentDigest, so ANY change here changes cache identity and must ship with an analyzer version bump. No analyzer may carry a private copy of these numbers.
_falseStartsComment: WHEN A REPEATED RUN COUNTS AS A FALSE START rather than an aside.
A false start -- saying a piece of the script, stopping, saying it again --
appears in the alignment as a run of insertions sitting beside the script
region then said properly. Most insertion runs are NOT false starts: they
are ad-libs, filler, an aside. What separates a restart is that the
abandoned run RESEMBLES what follows it, IN ORDER.
800/1000 is CHOSEN, NOT MEASURED, and errs HIGH deliberately. This is
evidence, and evidence that cries wolf is worse than none: a reviewer who
learns the false-start list is mostly wrong stops reading it, and the real
ones become invisible too. Too high merely misses some; too low destroys
the signal. falseStartCount is recorded on every alignment so this gets
corrected from real recordings rather than staying an estimate -- the same
treatment the pacing block and the caption spelling floor carry.
minTokens 2 refuses one-word runs outright: a single repeated word is a
stutter or a filler, not a restart, and reporting those would bury the real
ones in noise.
THESE LIVE HERE, NOT IN edit_policy_v1.json. That file is the COMPILER's
authority; this one is the ANALYSIS stage's, and the alignment component is
built in the analysis stage. They also enter alignmentEffectiveConfig and
therefore the component DIGEST, because they change the evidence produced --
without that, retuning a threshold would silently reuse a record computed
under the old one, which is a cache hit returning the wrong answer.
